basis: Defining craniosynostosis and acanthosis; hydrocephalus 3/4, choanal atresia 30-79%. Hearing loss and ocular inflammation each 30-79% omitted under cap, prioritizing CNS and airway severity.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: choanal atresia causes direct airway obstruction in 30-79%; prioritized under the cap because of potentially severe airway compromise.
decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing loss in 30-79% qualifies, but the four-axis cap prioritizes defining skeletal/skin disease, hydrocephalus and airway obstruction.

basis: Deafness, synostoses and neurodevelopmental defects define syndrome; urethral hypospadias 80-99%. Alopecia and dental anomalies, each 30-79%, omitted under cap; only two reported patients.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral defect, within the renal axis, reported in 80-99%; it is not solely a reproductive abnormality.
decisions.dermatologic: none: alopecia in 30-79% qualifies but is excluded by the cap in favor of more frequent urethral malformation; abnormal dermatoglyphics alone do not establish damage.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease; refractive impairment, chronic bowel dysfunction/dental malposition and foot deformities each 80-99% in supplied HPO. Central breathing spells do not establish lung damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: persistent intestinal dysmotility causes functional impairment; constipation and dental malposition are annotated 80-99%, reflux 4/4.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent pes valgus in 80-99% and pes planus in 4/4 represent common structural foot deformities, beyond neurologic hypotonia alone.

basis: Preformed toxin blocks neuromuscular transmission; ocular, autonomic and respiratory signs reflect neural blockade. [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/botulism/)

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inhalational botulism is intoxication by preformed toxin, without infection or immune-mediated disease; bacterial ancestry does not establish an infectious mechanism.

basis: Defining cardiac/visceral malformations: cardiac defects 2/2, asplenia and malrotation each 1/1; developmental delay 1/1 supports neurologic involvement. Bronchial isomerism alone adds no lung damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: splenic maldevelopment, including asplenia reported in 1/1, is a defining visceral heterotaxy abnormality; spleen belongs to the haematologic axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal malrotation is part of the defining visceral malformation pattern, reported in 1/1. [Case](https://doi.org/10.1101/mcs.a006248)

basis: Diaphragm defect, respiratory impairment with pulmonary hypoplasia, and persistent pulmonary hypertension define disease. Malrotation 30-79% alone does not establish common bowel dysfunction.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: persistent pulmonary hypertension is explicitly defining; it affects pulmonary arteries, which belong to cardiovascular.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: respiratory insufficiency is explicitly defining, supported by pulmonary hypoplasia in 30-79%; this is direct lung underdevelopment.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: malrotation occurs in 30-79%, but common bowel injury or functional loss is unproven. [Cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31200390/)

basis: Defining cardiac/pericardial, sternal, diaphragmatic and abdominal wall defects; pulmonary hypoplasia 30-79%. Omphalocele is an abdominal wall defect without established intrinsic bowel damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the defining omphalocele is an abdominal wall defect; herniated bowel location alone does not establish bowel disease or dysfunction.

basis: Limb/jaw dysostosis, splenic fusion and oral malformations define syndrome. Individual oral HPO findings are 5-29%; lung/cardiac defects also 5-29%; unspecified skin findings lack damage evidence.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate and microglossia belong to the defining orofacial phenotype; mouth is gastrointestinal, despite individual oral HPO frequencies of 5-29%.

basis: Arthritis and colitis/parotitis each 1/2; hepatic deposits lack proven dysfunction; otitis mechanism uncertain. [Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38609546/)

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: biopsy-proven inflammatory colitis and parotitis in 1/2 reported patients (~50%) are direct manifestations of autoinflammation; small cohort limits certainty.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: severe inflammatory arthritis in 1/2 reported patients (~50%), with synovial inflammation and impaired ambulation, directly damages joint function.

basis: Developmental delay and callosal defects define syndrome; renal dysplasia/cysts 2/3 and clubfoot 2/4. Respiratory insufficiency 3/4 lacks evidence of direct lung disease; cardiac defects each 1/4.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 3/4 is frequent, but its mechanism and persistence are unspecified; no direct lung or airway lesion is established.
